**Test image observations:**
- Patches of wilting/dying soybean plants amid otherwise healthy green canopy
- Affected plants show yellowing/chlorosis progressing to complete browning and death
- Dead plants have leaves/petioles still attached even after plant death
- The disease appears in discrete patches, not uniform across the field
- Progression visible from yellowing (middle) to fully dead/brown plants (right side)

**Reasoning:**
The field-level patch pattern with plants progressing from chlorosis → wilting → complete death with leaves/petioles remaining attached is highly characteristic of **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)**. The SDS reference confirms: patches of dying plants in an otherwise healthy canopy, interveinal chlorosis on leaves, and petioles persisting on dead stems. The visible pattern in the test image — healthy green neighbors, discrete dying patches, retained petioles on dead stems — matches SDS over alternatives like Phytophthora (which shows a stem lesion progressing from soil line) or SCN (which shows stunting without rapid death).
